newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares close up, buoyed by Droga.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares close up, buoyed by Droga.

text.p: Slovenian shares firmed one percent on Wednesday, pulled up by food maker Droga, and dealers forecast selective demand would characterise trade in the short term.
The SBI index rose 13.18 points to 1,318.96 reversing some of the week's decline.
"Food and drug producers are the most interesting shares on this market due to their good business performance and future outlook," a trader said.
Droga was the top gainer, firming 1.78 percent to 28,000 tolars on volume of 49 shares.
Another food maker, Kolinska was the most active traded stock. Its shares fell 0.52 percent to 1,900 tolars on volume of 13,683 for total turnover of 26.1 million tolars.
Brokerage Dadas led the day's decliners, tumbling 9.68 percent to 7,000 tolars on volume of 69 shares. Traders said the fall was a correction after Tuesday's strong gains.
Overall seven shares rose, six fell and two were flat, while 13 were untraded. Turnover fell to 84.0 million tolars, from 106.8 million tolars.
Dealers held out the hope that parliament's long-awaited ratification of an association accord with the European Union, expected next week, would stimulate trade in the longer term.
